A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
endothelium dependent vascular relaxation is significantly impaired in pregnant women with hypertension and this effect is more pronounced in patients with higher arterial blood pressure.

in women with hypertension during gestation there was a significant lowering of function of endothelum, elevation of FW and resistance index in utero feto-placental arteries, and these changes were improved at the background of antihypertensive therapy.

the endothelium of brachial artery in women with arterial hypertension during pregnancy is damaged, and this damage is progressing with elevation of blood pressure level, and treatment with nifedypine SR/GITS or bisoprolol is improving endothelial function.
The main takeaway from our work is that
in pregnant women with stage I-II hypertension we observed endothelial dysfunction and disturbances of blood flow in utero feto-placental system which can be improved with treatment.

in pregnant women with stage of II hypertension there is a significant endothelial dysfunction and utero fetic placental hypoperfusion which is improved with the use of nifedypine SR/GITS or bisoprolol in combination.
in pregnant women with stage 2 hypertension there is significant endothelial dysfunction, expressed by lowering of EDVD and elevation of FW level.
